title: AuthenticatorType
description: An Authenticator type's declarative manifest: how tools authenticate to a kind of Target. It names the secret slots a Credential fills with Secrets (each written by the Runner as a file or set as a variable), the non-secret params, the tools it needs, how a check and the capability report's usage name the material, the check that proves the identity, and the query that proves what it may do. Nothing acquires, refreshes, or revokes: the material comes with the Job. The builtin types are compiled into internal/authn and read-only through the API: k8s.kubeconfig, http.api_key, aws.keys, ambient, registry.docker_config.

version.description: Incremented on every change a Credential's params or checks could notice.

interactive.description: The type needs a human (device code, browser SSO); a Job cannot use it, and the Hub refuses a Credential of it for Jobs.

secrets.description: The slots a Credential fills with Secrets of its Environment, by name.

env.description: Non-secret variables set for the Credential's checks and for the work, as templates of {params.x} (AWS_DEFAULT_REGION from params.region). A template whose parameter is absent sets nothing.

params.description: JSON Schema (2020-12) for the Credential's params. Never secret.

git.description: Git over HTTPS with the Credential: the Runner sets git's credential helper for https://<host> in the work's git configuration, answering username and the value of the variable password_env names, so git clone and fetch work and the token is never on a command line.

host.description: The host (and port), a template of {params.x}.

requires_tools.description: Binaries the checks and the tools need on the Runner image's PATH; may use {params.x}. A missing one is an error on the check, named, not a failed Job.

requires_network.description: Hosts the tools reach, with {params.x} placeholders: what the operator's network policy must allow. Declarative; nothing enforces it.

usage.description: How to use the Credential, for the capability report's how-to-use column and the agent's brief, as a template of {params.x} and {credential.name}. Never secret.

guide.description: How an agent works with a Credential of this type, in Markdown, for its brief: the tool's forms that use it, worked examples, and the pitfalls (how to pass a script, what not to retry). A template of {params.x} and {credential.name}. Never secret. The Runner adds on its own what the Credential sets (each variable and file, by name) and, for a write Credential, how ops act runs a command, so the guide does not repeat them.

permissions_hint.description: What to grant and which Secrets to fill, for the UI and MCP (every type ships it).

AuthenticatorPreflight.title: AuthenticatorPreflight
AuthenticatorPreflight.description: Section 10.1 preflight: authn proves the identity (its expect.json value is the report's identity); authz is the type's own allow check, run before the Credential's authz_checks; authz_query is the provider's authorization query every Credential authz check must be.

AuthzQuery.title: AuthzQuery
AuthzQuery.description: The provider's authorization query (a can-i style query). Every Credential authz check of this type must start with prefix (placeholders as in run) and may pass after it only the flags listed (a flag's value after = or as the next word), so a check cannot run another command with the material or send it elsewhere. The Hub refuses others at save and the Runner refuses them again.

flags.description: Flags allowed after the prefix; each takes a value when it ends with =.

AuthenticatorVariants.title: AuthenticatorVariants
AuthenticatorVariants.description: Per-value overrides chosen by one param (ambient's tool: aws, gcloud, az, vault). The param must be an enum in params with a default or be required; the chosen value's fields replace the manifest's.
